mutation_rule: Do not infer a failure mechanism, affected type, exclusion, preservation guarantee, implementation route, or unchanged-output assertion from the reported example. Discover the actual behavioral boundary and expected fixed semantics from repository evidence, or obtain explicit owner approval; separately resolve any implementation choice that changes observable behavior. Add acceptance cases only when evidenced, approved, or clearly non-contractual.
change_summary: Adds a single boundary-and-semantics rule preventing unsupported narrowing, invented preservation requirements, mechanism assumptions, and mandatory test expansion while requiring observable technical choices to be resolved.

signal_reviews.reason: The acceptance assertion imposed unchanged output without repository evidence or owner approval and contradicted correct fixed semantics.
The contract invented a specific failure mechanism and required guard instead of discovering or owner-deciding the actual matching boundary.
The unchanged-form requirement was unsupported and excluded valid recursive behavior that repository testing should have exposed.
A broad non-match boundary was selected without evidence or an owner decision despite changing compatible recursive behavior.
The dependency ambiguity was explicitly resolved by the owner, who approved adding no declaration.
The compatibility difference was bounded, disclosed, and explicitly owner-approved.
The observable hook-cardinality change was disclosed and explicitly accepted by the owner.
The implementation routes have different observable scope and output, yet the contract neither selected one through evidence or approval nor established a constrained delegation boundary.
The GenericAlias-only boundary was an unsupported narrowing that excluded the repository's ordinary class-alias failure.
The preservation guarantee for generated alias text contradicted the required documented-alias behavior and lacked supporting evidence or approval.
The non-GenericAlias exclusion created an unsupported compatibility boundary that prevented resolution of the audited regression.
The contract elevated additional alias shapes and formatting scenarios into mandatory coverage without request, repository evidence, or owner approval.
Retaining generated alias text was an invented preservation requirement contrary to the requested replacement semantics and expected regression behavior.

The delegated coercion mechanism can change denominator dtype and backend behavior, so the contract needed either an approved choice or an explicit delegation boundary constraining those observable effects.
